findings.reason: an implementer taking "10 to 27" at face value would look for an 18-member source that does not exist and mistarget the split, whereas "10 to 34" is what the node's own live check ("flux loop 7 alone, the 26 differential loops in one source") and the cited inventory fragment require.
findings.text: §9 states "loops 1 to 9 are one-member sources and loops 10 to 27 share one 25-member source", but loops 10 to 27 are eighteen loops, not twenty-five, and the plan's own §6 (line 318) says the EDAS holds 34 loop channels. The `sensor-geometry-inventory` fragment (docs/evidence/fragments/signal-cocos-conventions/sensor-geometry-inventory.html:26) settles it: "27 / 7 of 34 graph channels … Ten source groups: nine fully covered, one partially covered (18 joined, 7 unjoined members)", so the single multi-member group is loops 10 through 34 (25 members), of which only 18 have deck rows and 7 (28–34) do not. The `measurement-kind-sources` regroup must therefore split a 25-member source of loops 10–34, leaving the 7 deck-row-less loops unmoved — not the 18-member group the sentence as written describes.

findings.reason: "the same module" most plainly means `imas_codex/discovery/static/geometry.py` from `sensor-geometry-graph`, so the intent is discoverable; naming it explicitly would remove the ambiguity but not alter the design.
findings.text: the `jt60sa-sensor-geometry` node ingests the SELENE decks "through the same module" and cross-checks against imas-ambix over 2 h, but its only declared write path is the evidence fragment `docs/evidence/fragments/signal-cocos-conventions/jt60sa-sensor-geometry.html`; the code it must add (the deck reader it defers to by the phrase "beside the module's deck reader") has no declared write path, so the implementer is left to place code in an undeclared file.
